verses.text: Now farewell, you who live in the halls of Olympus,
and you islands and mainlands, and the salt sea between them.
Now sing of the family of goddesses, sweet-voiced
Muses of Olympus, daughters of Zeus who carries the aegis,
all those who slept beside mortal men
and, though immortal, bore children like gods.
Demeter, radiant among goddesses, bore Plutus
after joining the hero Iasion in sweet love
in a field plowed three times, in the fertile land of Crete,
kindly Plutus, who travels over the earth and the sea’s broad back,
everywhere. Whoever meets him, whoever’s hands he comes into,
he makes rich and grants great wealth.
Harmonia, daughter of golden Aphrodite, bore Cadmus
Ino and Semele and lovely-cheeked Agave,
and Autonoe, whom Aristaeus with his thick hair married,
and Polydorus, in Thebes with its beautiful crown.
Callirhoe, daughter of Oceanus, joined strong-hearted Chrysaor
in love through Aphrodite, rich in gold,
and bore a son, the strongest of all mortals,
Geryon, whom mighty Heracles killed
for his cattle with their rolling gait, on Erytheia, surrounded by the sea.
Eos bore Tithonus Memnon in his bronze helmet,
king of the Ethiopians, and lord Emathion.
With Cephalus, Eos brought forth a glorious son,
mighty Phaethon, a man like the gods.
While Phaethon was young, in the tender flower of glorious youth,
a boy with a carefree heart, smile-loving Aphrodite
swept him away and, in her most sacred temples,
made him her attendant by night, a glorious divine spirit.
Medea, daughter of King Aeetes, whom Zeus sustained,
was led away by Jason, Aeson’s son, by the will of the gods who live forever,
away from Aeetes, once Jason had finished the painful trials,
the many tasks imposed by the great, overbearing king,
Pelias, violent and reckless, whose deeds were brutal.
After finishing those trials and suffering greatly, Jason reached Iolcus,
bringing the bright-eyed girl aboard his swift ship,
and Jason, Aeson’s son, made her his wife in the bloom of youth.
Medea, joined in love with Jason, shepherd of his people,
bore a son, Medeius, whom Chiron raised in the mountains,
Chiron, son of Philyra. And great Zeus’s plan was fulfilled.
Then came the daughters of Nereus, the old man of the sea:
Psamathe, radiant among goddesses, bore Phocus
after joining Aeacus in love through golden Aphrodite;
and the silver-footed goddess Thetis joined Peleus
and bore Achilles, who broke through men’s ranks and had a lion’s heart.
Aphrodite, with her beautiful crown, bore Aeneas
after joining the hero Anchises in sweet love
on the heights of wooded Mount Ida with its many folds.
Circe, daughter of Helios, the son of Hyperion,
joined patient-hearted Odysseus in love and bore
Agrius and Latinus, a man both noble and strong.
She also bore Telegonus through golden Aphrodite.
Far, far away, deep among the sacred islands,
they ruled over all the famous Tyrrhenians.
Calypso, radiant among goddesses, bore Odysseus Nausithous
and Nausinous after joining him in sweet love.
These were the goddesses who slept beside mortal men
and, though immortal, bore children like gods.
Now sing of the family of women, sweet-voiced
Muses of Olympus, daughters of Zeus who carries the aegis.

uncertainties: Verse 1014 is marked for deletion in the supplied Greek. Its words are translated here because every assigned verse requires an item.
The epithet for the cattle in verse 983 has an uncertain sense, traditionally rendered as describing a rolling or shambling gait.
